card.one_liner: Variance tolerances, approval limits, duplicate invoices that change one letter, and month-end cutoffs.

rules.text: Every invoice needs a three-way match: purchase order, receipt, invoice.
Approval limits are 5,000 dollars for a team lead and 25,000 for a director.
No purchase order, no payment, for anything above 1,000 dollars.
Credit notes apply to the invoice they reference, never to the oldest open item.

exceptions.text: Freight invoices: accept variance up to 3% or 50 dollars, whichever is larger; above that, route to the buyer with the surcharge table.
Fixed-price service contracts get zero tolerance; any variance means the scope changed.
Utility or tax invoices with a shutoff or penalty date within 5 days are paid without a PO and flagged as exception.
At month-end cutoff, split a multi-cost-centre invoice by PO lines rather than returning it; a return understates expenses.

judgment_calls.text: Search duplicates by vendor and amount within 90 days, not by invoice number; vendors reissue with -A or -REV suffixes.
A team lead approving an invoice for a vendor they own the relationship with is a hold, regardless of amount.
When a PO is 'coming', hold and copy the buyer; pay within 2 days of the PO number arriving.

common_mistakes.text: Paying on an approval stamp without checking the approver's limit; a 12,000 dollar invoice approved by a team lead is invalid.
Applying a credit note to the wrong open invoice, turning a one-hour statement reconciliation into a full day.
Posting a duplicate because the vendor changed one character of the invoice number.

never_do.text: Never pay an invoice above 1,000 dollars without a PO on a verbal promise; refuse and ask for the PO number.
Never return a month-end invoice to the vendor if it means missing the accrual cutoff.
Never approve a variance on a fixed-price contract.
